paper_metadata.title: Microstructure regulation and strength-elongation synergy of the near alpha TZAM alloy via thermomechanical processing

evidence.quote: the relationship between the microstructure evolution and mechanical properties of the Ti-25Zr-4Al-1.5Mn (TZAM, wt. %) near- α Ti alloy was systematically investigated after hot rolling at temperatures ranging in the whole solid solution region.
an obvious yield strength-elongation synergy was obtained for this TZAM alloy by using the simple method of hot rolling.

To prevent oxidation during the smelting process, the alloys were melted under an argon atmosphere using Zr as an oxygen absorber in a vacuum non-consumable electric arc furnace. Each ingot had a controlled mass of approximately 75 g.

parameters.time: 30 min initial heating; 4 min re-heating before each pass; 4 min final hold

evidence.quote: Each TZAM sample was then heated in the furnace at the corresponding temperature for 30 min before undergoing multi-pass rolling using a two-high mill. During rolling, the samples were re-heated at the corresponding temperatures for 4 min before the next pass of rolling. The pressure applied during each pass was approximately 1.2 mm, with the total deformation reaching 88.5 % of the original ingot thickness.
Once the desired thickness was achieved, the ingot was placed in the furnace for 4 min and then rapidly quenched.
